title: Skip counting with equal hops

explain.say: You can count socks in pairs: 2, 4, 6, 8. That is skip counting. Look at the number line. The hops start at 0. Each hop is 2, all the way to 20.
Look at the hops from 0: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, up to 20. That is 10 equal hops of 2. Every number you land on is even.
Now hop in 5s from 0: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. You can count fingers this way, one hand at a time. How many hops of 5 reach 25?
Now hop in 10s from 0: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. Just 5 hops reach 50. Counting in 10s helps you count coins of 10 quickly. What comes after 50?
Skip counting helps you learn times tables. Look at hops of 3 from 0: 3, 6, 9, up to 30. That is 10 threes. Can you count in 3s to 30?

faq.a: Skip counting means counting forward by the same number each time, skipping the numbers in between. Counting 2, 4, 6, 8 is skip counting in 2s.
Start at 0 and add 5 each time: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. The numbers always end in 5 or 0.
Lots of things come in pairs, like socks, shoes and eyes. Counting in 2s is twice as fast as counting in 1s.

faq.q: How is skip counting like times tables?
faq.a: Each hop is one more group. 4 hops of 5 land on 20, and 4 times 5 is 20. Skip counting builds the times tables.
asks: Is skip counting the same as multiplying?

faq.q: What pattern is in counting in 10s?
faq.a: Counting in 10s from 0, every number ends in 0, and the tens digit goes up by 1 each time: 10, 20, 30, 40.
asks: Why do the 10s all end in 0?

facts: Counting in 2s from 0 lands only on even numbers.
Counting in 5s from 0, every number ends in 5 or 0.

wrong.2: 25 comes after 20. You skipped a hop.

quiz.say: Hop in 10s from 0. How many hops reach 60?
quiz.show: Hops of 10 from 0 to 60. How many hops?
quiz.why: Count the hops: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. That is 6 hops.

wrong.0: 60 is where you land. Count the hops.
wrong.1: 10 is the size of each hop. Count the hops.
